title: Residue degree and value-group index are bounded by the valued field degree
statement: Let $F\subseteq H$ be fields [def-weil-field] with compatible real-valued nonarchimedean absolute values: $|x|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $|xy|=|x||y|$, $|1|=1$, and $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$. Neither completeness nor a discrete valuation is assumed. For $M=F,H$ put $M^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$, a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\mathfrak m_M=\{x:|x|<1\}$, $\widetilde M=M^\circ/\mathfrak m_M$, and $\Gamma_M=|M^\times|\subset\mathbf R_{>0}$. The inclusions give embeddings $\widetilde F\hookrightarrow\widetilde H$ and $\Gamma_F\hookrightarrow\Gamma_H$. Assume $H$ has finite dimension $n\ge1$ as an $F$-vector space. Then the residue extension has finite dimension $f=[\widetilde H:\widetilde F]$, the quotient group $\Gamma_H/\Gamma_F$ has a finite number $e=[\Gamma_H:\Gamma_F]$ of cosets, and $ef\le n$.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp. 7–8, the fundamental inequality immediately before Lemma 2.1.2; primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $M=F,H$, the absolute-value identities show that $M^\circ$ is a subring and that $\mathfrak m_M$ is a proper ideal: sums of two elements of norm $<1$ still have norm $<1$, and multiplication by an element of norm $\le1$ preserves this inequality. An element of $M^\circ$ outside this ideal has norm $1$, hence its inverse also belongs to $M^\circ$; conversely a unit has norm $1$. Thus the quotient is a field. For $x\ne0$, either $|x|\le1$ or $|x^{-1}|<1$, giving the valuation-ring condition of [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Every element of $M$ is a fraction of elements of $M^\circ$: if $|x|>1$, use $x=1/x^{-1}$. Compatibility gives $F^\circ=F\cap H^\circ$ and $\mathfrak m_F=F\cap\mathfrak m_H$, so the induced residue homomorphism is injective. The value groups are subgroups under multiplication, since norms preserve products and inverses, and their inclusion is injective.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, lemma-inequality-general, proof; valuation-ring extension terminology: Tag 0ASG, definition-extension-valuation-rings.

proof.text:
Fix positive integers $r,s$, independent residue classes $ ar b_1,\ldots, ar b_r\in\widetilde H$ over $\widetilde F$, and $c_1,\ldots,c_s\in H^	imes$ whose norms represent distinct cosets modulo $\Gamma_F$. Lift each $ ar b_i$ to $b_i\in H^\circ$. Each class is nonzero, so $|b_i|=1$. For coefficients $a_{ij}\in F$ not all zero, choose $(i_0,j_0)$ maximizing $|a_{ij}c_j|$, and put $a_0=a_{i_0j_0}
e0$. Divide the putative relation $\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}b_ic_j=0$ by $a_0c_{j_0}$. Every resulting term has norm at most $1$. If $j
e j_0$ and a nonzero term had norm $1$, then $|c_j|/|c_{j_0}|=|a_0/a_{ij}|\in\Gamma_F$, contradicting the distinct cosets. Thus every term with $j
e j_0$ has norm strictly less than $1$.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, lemma-inequality-general, proof; valuation-ring extension terminology: Tag 0ASG, definition-extension-valuation-rings.

proof.text: For $j=j_0$ the normalized coefficient is $a_{ij_0}/a_0\in F^\circ$, and its value for $i=i_0$ is $1$. Reduce the normalized relation in $H^\circ/\mathfrak m_H$. The terms with $j\ne j_0$ vanish; reduction of the others gives $\sum_i\overline{a_{ij_0}/a_0}\,\bar b_i=0$, with coefficients in the embedded field $\widetilde F$ and the $i_0$ coefficient equal to $1$. This contradicts independence of the $\bar b_i$. Reduction commutes with this finite sum and with its products because it is a quotient-ring homomorphism. Hence the $rs$ elements $b_ic_j$ are linearly independent over $F$.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, lemma-inequality-general, proof; valuation-ring extension terminology: Tag 0ASG, definition-extension-valuation-rings.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-independent-family-card-le-dimension] to the finite independent family $(b_ic_j)_{(i,j)\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\times\{1,\ldots,s\}}$ in the $n$-dimensional $F$-vector space $H$. The index set has $rs$ elements, so $rs\le n$. This holds for every finite residue-independent family and every finite family of distinct value cosets chosen in Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, lemma-inequality-general, concluding dimension bound; Mathlib LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finite.lean:161–164.

proof.text: Take $s=1$ and $c_1=1$. Step 4 bounds every finite independent family in $\widetilde H$ over $\widetilde F$ by $n$. Start with the empty family and, whenever its span is not all of $\widetilde H$, append an element outside the span. Independence is preserved: a relation with a nonzero coefficient on the appended element would express it in the old span, and if that coefficient is zero the old independence applies. The process must stop by the $n$th choice, since otherwise it constructs $n+1$ independent elements. It therefore produces a finite basis of size $f$, with $1\le f\le n$ because the residue field has $1\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, lemma-inequality-general, proof; valuation-ring extension terminology: Tag 0ASG, definition-extension-valuation-rings.

proof.text: Take $r=1$ and $\bar b_1=\bar1$. If $\Gamma_H/\Gamma_F$ contained $n+1$ distinct cosets, choose a representative in $\Gamma_H$ for each and then an element of $H^\times$ with that norm. Step 4 would give $n+1\le n$. Thus the coset set is finite of cardinality $e\le n$, and $e\ge1$ because it contains the identity coset. Explicitly, successive choices of a coset outside those already selected terminate after at most $n$ choices, and then exhaust the quotient.

source.place: Tag 0ASH, lemma-inequality-general, proof; valuation-ring extension terminology: Tag 0ASG, definition-extension-valuation-rings.

proof.text: Choose the residue basis of size $f$ obtained in Step 5 and representatives in $H^\times$ for all $e$ cosets obtained in Step 6. Apply the finite-family bound of Step 4 with $r=f$ and $s=e$, which are positive. It gives $fe\le n$, hence $ef\le n$. Together with Steps 5 and 6 this proves both finiteness assertions and the required inequality.
